name: A: Learnable noise dampening
theory: Fixed AR(1) z_{t+1} = 0.8*z_t + 0.6*eps creates positive autocorrelation in deltas, causing super-diffusive spread at h=7-30. Replace with learned z_{t+1} = f(cond)*z_t + g(cond)*eps where f,g are small MLPs conditioned on encoder output. This allows the model to learn mean-reverting noise dynamics (f < 1) that match GT negative autocorrelation.
target: Suite 2 (CI coverage) — fix per-horizon over-spread at h=7-30
prediction: Per-horizon CI should tighten. Lag-1 ACF of deltas should shift from +0.25..+0.83 toward GT -0.35..-0.51.
risk: May destabilize noise process if f grows unbounded. Need sigmoid/tanh clamping on f to keep in [0, 1]. Also rho=0.0 ablation (101a) showed losing noise correlation breaks growing uncertainty — so f should NOT go to 0.
implementation: Add LearnableARNoise module: f = sigmoid(MLP_f(condition)), g = softplus(MLP_g(condition)). Replace fixed rho in AR loop. Init f near 0.8.

name: B: Encoder-modulated per-cell noise scale
theory: REDUNDANT with cell_spread — proven by Exp 102a. Both are condition→25 scalars on same path. CRPS per-cell gradient pulls both toward uniform.
finding: 102a: noise_scale learned only 1.4x range (GT: 35x). Kurtosis regressed 0.845→0.605. Better calibration (0.072→0.043) but doesn't flip any suite.

name: C: Non-anchored dynamics / level prediction
theory: Additive iv_t = prev + vs*delta anchors all trajectories to history[-1]. After 30 steps, distribution of levels is tightly centered around drift from anchor. GT levels at h=30 have much wider distribution. KS on IV levels fails 0-1/25 because the level distribution never departs enough from the anchor. A level-correction head or mean-reverting target could break this anchor dependency.
prediction: KS on IV levels should improve from 0-1/25. Level distribution should widen.
risk: May break surface validity if level predictions are noisy. May conflict with per-step CRPS that rewards accurate per-step predictions (which favor anchoring).
implementation: Options: (a) Horizon-dependent drift head that predicts cumulative level offset. (b) Mean-reversion to learned long-run mean. (c) Level-matching loss at select horizons. Start with (a) as most Bitter-Lesson compatible.
